# bbw: Blocked Weighted Bootstrap

## Overview

The **blocked weighted bootstrap** is an estimation technique for use
with data from two-stage cluster sampled surveys in which either prior
weighting (e.g. *population-proportional sampling* or *PPS* as used in
Standardized Monitoring and Assessment of Relief and Transitions or
SMART surveys) or *posterior weighting* (e.g. as used in [Rapid
Assessment Method (RAM)](https://rapidsurveys.io/ramOPmanual/) and
[Simple Spatial Sampling Method
(S3M)](https://researchonline.lshtm.ac.uk/id/eprint/2572543) surveys) is
implemented.

## Installation

You can install the latest development version of
[bbw](https://github.com/rapidsurveys/bbw) through GitHub via the
[pak](https://pak.r-lib.org/) package with:

``` r
if (!require(pak)) install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rapidsurveys/bbw")
```

You can also install [bbw](https://github.com/rapidsurveys/bbw) from the
[RapidSurveys R Universe](https://rapidsurveys.r-universe.dev) with:

``` r
install.packages(
  "bbw", 
  repos = c(
    "https://rapidsurveys.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)
```

## Usage

[bbw](https://github.com/rapidsurveys/bbw) as used in RAM and S3M is a
modification to the *percentile bootstrap* to include *blocking* and
*weighting* to account for a *complex sample design*.

With RAM and S3M surveys, the sample is complex in the sense that it is
an unweighted cluster sample. Data analysis procedures need to account
for the sample design. A blocked weighted bootstrap can be used:

  

- **Blocked**: The block corresponds to the primary sampling unit (*PSU
  = cluster*). PSUs are resampled with replacement. Observations within
  the resampled PSUs are also sampled with replacement.

- **Weighted**: RAM and S3M samples do not use population proportional
  sampling (PPS) to weight the sample prior to data collection (e.g. as
  is done with SMART surveys). This means that a posterior weighting
  procedure is required. [bbw](https://github.com/rapidsurveys/bbw) uses
  a *“roulette wheel”* algorithm (see [illustration below](#fig1)) to
  weight (i.e. by population) the selection probability of PSUs in
  bootstrap replicates.

![Roulette wheel algorithm](reference/figures/rouletteWheel.png)

In the case of prior weighting by PPS all clusters are given the same
weight. With posterior weighting (as in RAM or S3M) the weight is the
population of each PSU. This procedure is very similar to the [*fitness
proportional
selection*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_proportionate_selection)
technique used in *evolutionary computing*.

A total of `m` PSUs are sampled with replacement for each bootstrap
replicate (where `m` is the number of PSUs in the survey sample).

The required statistic is applied to each replicate. The reported
estimate consists of the 0.025th (*95% LCL*), 0.5th (*point estimate*),
and 0.975th (*95% UCL*) quantiles of the distribution of the statistic
across all survey replicates.

The main reason to use [bbw](https://github.com/rapidsurveys/bbw) is
that the bootstrap allows a wider range statistics to be calculated than
model-based techniques without resort to grand assumptions about the
sampling distribution of the required statistic. A good example for this
is the confidence interval on the difference between two medians which
might be used for many socio-economic variables. The
[bbw](https://github.com/rapidsurveys/bbw) also allows for a wider range
of hypothesis tests to be used with complex sample survey data.

## Citation

If you use the [bbw](https://github.com/rapidsurveys/bbw) package in
your work, please cite using the suggested citation provided by a call
to the [`citation()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/citation.html) function as
follows:

``` r
citation("bbw")
#> To cite bbw in publications use:
#> 
#>   Mark Myatt, Ernest Guevarra (2026). _bbw: Blocked Weighted
#>   Bootstrap_. doi:10.5281/zenodo.6594797
#>   <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6594797>, R package version 0.3.1,
#>   <https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/>.
#> 
#> A BibTeX entry for LaTeX users is
#> 
#>   @Manual{,
#>     title = {bbw: Blocked Weighted Bootstrap},
#>     author = {{Mark Myatt} and {Ernest Guevarra}},
#>     year = {2026},
#>     note = {R package version 0.3.1},
#>     url = {https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/},
#>     doi = {10.5281/zenodo.6594797},
#>   }
```

# Package index

## Description

- [`bbw-package`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/bbw.md)
  [`bbw`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/bbw.md) : Blocked
  Weighted Bootstrap

## Bootstrap resampling

- [`bootBW()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/bootBW.md) :
  Blocked Weighted Bootstrap
- [`boot_bw()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/boot_bw.md)
  [`boot_bw_parallel()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/boot_bw.md)
  [`boot_bw_sequential()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/boot_bw.md)
  [`boot_bw_weight()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/boot_bw.md)
  [`boot_bw_sample_clusters()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/boot_bw.md)
  [`boot_bw_sample_within_clusters()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/boot_bw.md)
  : Blocked Weighted Bootstrap - vectorised and parallel
- [`boot_bw_estimate()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/boot_bw_estimate.md)
  : Estimate median and confidence intervals from bootstrap replicates

## Bootstrap statistic

- [`bootClassic()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/bootClassic.md)
  : Simple proportion statistics function for bootstrap estimation
- [`bootPROBIT()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/bootPROBIT.md)
  : PROBIT statistics function for bootstrap estimation

## Stratified weighted estimation

- [`estimate_total()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/estimate_total.md)
  : Post-stratification analysis

## Utility

- [`recode()`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/recode.md) :
  Recode

## Datasets

- [`indicatorsCH1`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/indicatorsCH1.md)
  : Child Morbidity, Health Service Coverage, Anthropometry
- [`indicatorsCH2`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/indicatorsCH2.md)
  : Infant and Child Feeding Index
- [`indicatorsHH`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/indicatorsHH.md)
  : Mother Indicators Dataset
- [`villageData`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/villageData.md)
  : Cluster Population Weights Dataset
- [`somalia_population`](https://rapidsurveys.io/bbw/dev/reference/somalia_population.md)
  : Somalia regional population in 2022
